newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to probe alleged military abuses.
newsitem.headline: Peru to probe alleged military abuses.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori promised his government will probe charges of torture and abuses by the army's intelligence service, but denied the existence of paramilitary forces.

"We will investigate," Fujimori told a television interviewer late on Sunday when asked about charges by an army intelligence member who said she was tortured by her own colleagues for allegedly leaking secret information to the press.

Leonor La Rosa told another television programme that she was tortured by the Army Intelligence Service, which suspected she had leaked confidential files about alleged paramilitary plans to intimidate opposition politicians and journalists.
"They burned my hands, they tortured me ... with electricity," La Rosa said. She said she has lost feeling in both hands and one is paralysed.

While promising an investigation, Fujimori denied any paramilitary groups existed in Peru. Authorities say they believe a recent series of unusual attacks on opposition politicians and journalists were carried out by common criminals.

Two opposition legislators -- a right-winger and a left- winger, are demanding the creation of a congressional committee to investigate the case of La Rosa and of a second army intelligence member, also a woman, whose body was recently found decapitated and with no hands.
Peru's Pro-Human Rights Association said it will take La Rosa's case to international human rights organisations.
In his television interview, Fujimori also said he would order an official probe into allegations that the army has tortured and abused peasants while chasing Marxist rebels in the jungle.
"Those excesses are inadmissible and must be punished," he said.

Human rights groups say 38 people were wrongly arrested and tortured when the army swept through villages in Peru's central jungle last month. Fujimori said he would not allow a return to the past "when (the army) would enter villages and suspect that everyone was a terrorist."

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels are holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima since Dec. 17 to press their demands for the release of their 450 jailed comrades.
